title: Munich 1972 Olympic pictograms
lede: Otl Aicher’s sport pictograms: figures drawn only with circles and bars on a 45-degree and 90-degree grid.
summary: Otl Aicher and the Munich organizing committee’s visual design department, 1972.

creator.name: Otl Aicher and Abteilung XI für visuelle Gestaltung, Organisationskomitee der XX. Olympischen Spiele München

evidence.note: Downloaded two CC BY 1.0 photographs by Henning Schlottmann of the pictograms still on site in Munich ([swimming hall](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_games_1972_pictogramms_swimming_hall_0525.JPG), [Olympiazentrum station](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_games_1972_pictogramms_olympic_station_0877.JPG)) to a scratch folder and inspected them. Poster data read on eMuseum record 230065. No image is stored.

styles.note: Aicher applied the style’s grid and objectivity to a wayfinding system; the pictograms are geometry on a fixed angular grid, without illustration.

context: Otl Aicher co-founded and taught at the Ulm School of Design and led the design team of the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, overseeing its system of pictograms. [Wikipedia: Otl Aicher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otl_Aicher).

Wikipedia’s history-of-design article quotes Michael Bierut praising the pictograms for their elegance and clarity. [Wikipedia: History of graphic design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_graphic_design).

The Museum für Gestaltung Zürich holds the poster *Piktogramme – München 1972 – Montreal 1976* (concept Otl Aicher; offset, 84 × 59.5 cm, object 33-0114). [eMuseum object 230065](https://www.emuseum.ch/objects/230065).
observed: Each sign is a square panel in one flat color (light blue at the swimming hall, green at the station) with a white figure.
Heads are plain circles detached from the body; limbs and torsos are straight bars with rounded ends.
Bars run only at vertical, horizontal, and 45-degree angles. The runner’s legs and the footballer’s body are built from the same few angles.
The football is a white outline circle, the only outlined shape in the two station panels.
interpretation: The pictograms extend the style from type to symbols: a small set of parts on a fixed geometric grid produces a large family that stays consistent across sports and sites.
borrow: Build icons from a restricted kit: one circle size, one bar width, and only 0°, 45°, and 90° angles.
Separate the head or key element from the body with a gap so shapes read clearly at small size.
Use one flat background color per zone or category, and white for the symbol.

rights.statement: The pictograms remain in copyright. The Commons photographs are CC BY 1.0 and rely on German freedom of panorama; they show a copyrighted design, so no image is stored.
